implementation: dwgRW and dwgR expose an explicit per-read layer-byte-order selection. The default retains legacy little-endian behavior; the reader snapshots the selection at read start.

Both entity and object EED resolve only a nonzero 32-bit selected handle present in the layer table. The original physical bytes remain in the existing raw reference; missing, zero and wide references stay unresolved.
The converter adapter re-parses source frames using the same per-import selection. The CLI accepts --dwg-eed-layer-byte-order=big or little; FreeCAD-compatible invocation remains available.

Shared DXF XDATA validation refuses unresolved DWG layer handles instead of emitting their hexadecimal spelling as a layer name. A resolved numeric layer name cannot be mistaken for an unresolved handle. DWG raw replay remains separate.
validation: Generated R13/R14 little-endian, big-endian, missing, zero and wide controls test policy switching, invalid options, raw-byte preservation, explicit selection, partial DXF output, destination preservation and corrected retry.
Fresh ODA R13/R14/R2000 drawings were read under both policies, confirming the selected big-endian interpretation for entity and dictionary EED against ODA reopen.
Independent ezdxf 1.4.5 readback checks the selected layer name and actual layer table in both ASCII and Binary DXF for a locally generated control.

Focused ASan checks include CLI option parsing, EED text provenance, legacy dictionary/partial-output tests, and the existing exhaustive XDATA allocation rollback/retry sweep. The slow sweep is separate from the fast numeric test and sizes its search from the measured clean allocation count.
limits: Selection is explicit; the implementation does not infer producer identity or decide between conflicting byte orders.
This slice does not change DWG writer byte order, qualify automatic source profiles, certify broader DWG/DXF support, or replace native AutoCAD and platform evidence.
The ODA candidate controls check import, not full-document conversion: unrelated ModelDocViewStyle and native-qualification gates remain.
